active_paradigms.idea: Extract the jammed contact graph from the current alternating-corner solution and solve its active-distance equations with scipy.optimize.least_squares
active_paradigms.description: The current program starts from a 16-point subset of the radius-2 triangular lattice, normalizes its diameter, and then uses repeated COBYLA runs over all 30 coordinate variables plus a separation variable. Its main strength is that the lattice already has the correct dense-packing topology, which is why tiny continuous displacements reach the reference score. Its weakness is that COBYLA treats the many inactive pair constraints equally with the genuinely binding nearest-neighbor and diameter constraints, and its final coordinates retain feasibility/convergence noise. After one deterministic identification of pairs whose distances are within a tight tolerance of either dmin or dmax in the current best configuration, formulate residuals that force nearest pairs to a common squared distance t and diameter pairs to squared distance 1. Fix translation, rotation, and scale by pinning one point at the origin and another point on the x-axis at the identified diameter, then solve the resulting overdetermined active-set system with scipy.optimize.least_squares using very tight ftol, xtol, and gtol. Return the solution only if a full pdist verification confirms that no nominally inactive pair falls below the solved nearest distance or exceeds the diameter. This is a direct numerical polishing method rather than another exploratory local search, and it can remove the approximately 10^-6-level gap caused by COBYLA tolerances.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The squared min/max ratio directly, with particular emphasis on accurately equalizing all true shortest contacts and all true diameter contacts while retaining a strict safety margin for inactive pairs.
active_paradigms.cautions: The active graph must be inferred conservatively: include all nearly binding contacts, because omitting a true contact can produce a mathematically clean but infeasible solution. Use squared-distance residuals, normalize after solving, and validate every one of the 120 pairs with float64 before accepting. If the active equations are rank-deficient, retain enough gauge equations or add a small number of nearly active constraints rather than relying on arbitrary coordinate pinning.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.root on a square equilibrium system for the inferred optimal contact topology, including stress-balance equations
active_paradigms.description: The observed solution is a nearly jammed disk-packing configuration: its score above one indicates COBYLA has already found the intended local topology, but it does not explicitly impose stationarity of the max-min problem. Build the contact graph from the best deterministic lattice/COBYLA candidate, separating unit-diameter contacts from common-minimum-distance contacts. Introduce one scalar t and solve a square system consisting of selected contact equalities, gauge equations, and first-order equilibrium equations obtained from a nonnegative stress assignment on active contacts. The equilibrium conditions make the resulting coordinates stationary for the diameter-constrained packing problem, rather than merely feasible at COBYLA's stopping tolerance. Use scipy.optimize.root with method='lm' for an initially overdetermined formulation, or method='hybr' after reducing to an independent square basis, initialized from the existing candidate. The residual scale should use squared distances, with diameter equalities fixed to 1 and minimum equalities fixed to t. Finally calculate pdist and accept the root only if its actual minimum/maximum ratio improves the retained fallback. This approach exploits the geometric fact that an optimum should be infinitesimally rigid or have an equilibrium stress, which is information absent from the current black-box COBYLA objective.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical stationarity and rigidity of the current high-quality topology, aiming to obtain a reproducible ratio above the benchmark rather than a tolerance-dependent COBYLA result.
active_paradigms.cautions: A root solver does not enforce inequalities, so it must always be protected by a complete pairwise feasibility check and fallback. Contact-graph rank analysis is essential: redundant equations are useful with Levenberg-Marquardt, whereas HYBR requires an independent square system. Do not solve for arbitrary stresses unless their sign convention is checked; incorrect stress signs can converge to a non-maximal saddle configuration.

active_paradigms.idea: Run a deterministic low-dimensional topology search with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution over a symmetry-aware alternating-corner parameterization
active_paradigms.description: The present code searches 30 free coordinates locally and therefore has almost no chance of discovering a different contact topology that is marginally better than the triangular-lattice subset. Instead parameterize a family that preserves the evident alternating-corner/near-threefold structure: use a center point, several radial shell radii, angular offsets, and small independent perturbations for the three deleted-corner sectors, with one diameter-defining pair fixed by gauge. Define the objective as the negative actual squared ratio computed from all 120 pair distances, with a large deterministic penalty only when a coordinate parameterization degenerates; since the evaluator itself has no hard constraints beyond valid finite coordinates, direct ratio optimization exactly matches evaluation. Call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, workers=1, polish=True, and bounds that permit topology changes but exclude pathological collapse. Unlike COBYLA, this explores basin changes such as slightly non-lattice boundary spacing and altered hull point placement, while symmetry reduction makes global exploration feasible. The best returned parameter vector is expanded to all 16 points and compared against the existing lattice fallback by the evaluator’s exact pdist formula. If it finds a new topology, a later active-set solve can be used offline to understand it, but the submitted constructor should simply use the best deterministic result from this direct call.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escaping the current triangular-subset local basin to improve the primary squared ratio; the objective should be exactly min(pdist)^2/max(pdist)^2, not a surrogate separation variable.
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep the parameterization flexible enough that forced symmetry does not exclude the true optimum; include controlled sector-specific offsets rather than exact rotational symmetry. Differential evolution in 30 unrestricted coordinate dimensions is too expensive, so the dimensional reduction is central. Its finite runtime must be measured under the evaluator timeout, and every run must use a fixed seed and single-worker execution for deterministic output.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace COBYLA with a single analytic-Jacobian SLSQP solve of the epigraph formulation
tried_paradigms.description: The current program begins from a 16-site triangular-lattice patch with three alternating corners removed, normalizes its diameter, and uses several noisy COBYLA runs to maximize a separation variable subject to all pair distances being between the separation and one. This is strong because the lattice patch has the correct dense-packing topology and COBYLA can deform it into the known near-optimal non-lattice arrangement. Its main weakness is that COBYLA is derivative-free, is given 240 highly redundant inequalities, and the returned point is renormalized after optimization, so its optimized auxiliary variable is not exactly the evaluated ratio. Instead, fix translation and rotation by setting point 0=(0,0) and point 1=(1,0), optimize the remaining 28 coordinates plus t, and impose d_ij^2-t >= 0 and 1-d_ij^2 >= 0 directly. Use one deterministic start from the current best lattice/deformed coordinates and provide explicit dense analytic Jacobians for every squared-distance constraint and for the objective -t. SLSQP's active-set QP steps are much better matched to the small set of tight contacts in this packing than COBYLA's linear interpolation model. Return the coordinates directly without a post-solve normalization, because the fixed unit-diameter pair already fixes scale. After the solve, evaluate the exact pdist score and only retain a result with a small strict feasibility margin in the upper-distance constraints.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize t, which equals the evaluator's squared dmin/dmax ratio when the fixed pair remains a diameter pair. The target is to improve reliably beyond the approximately 0.077584 reference rather than merely exploiting COBYLA feasibility tolerance.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not optimize dmin/dmax through min/max inside the objective; use t and smooth individual inequalities. Include all 120 pair constraints in both directions of the epigraph formulation, use float64 analytic gradients, and set ftol substantially below 1e-11. SLSQP can falsely report success at a slightly infeasible point, so verify all distances before returning and shrink coordinates infinitesimally toward the anchor if any non-anchor distance exceeds one.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic differential evolution on an anchor-fixed, penalized global search formulation
tried_paradigms.description: The current method has excellent local geometry but all of its starts belong to one narrow lattice basin, so it can miss a different contact graph whose true ratio is higher. Construct a globally parameterized formulation by fixing two presumed diameter endpoints at (0,0) and (1,0), leaving 14 free points, and bounding each free point to the intersection-relevant square [0,1] x [-0.5,0.5] or a safely larger unit-disk bounding box. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on a deterministic seed and a vectorized objective that returns negative minimum squared pair distance plus a very large smooth penalty for any pair with squared distance above one. The objective should explicitly include distances to the two fixed anchors and between every free pair. This directly targets the evaluator statistic rather than an auxiliary t, while the fixed anchors remove translation, rotation, and scale degeneracies that otherwise waste most of a population search. The optimizer can use a large population and Sobol initialization so that it tests contact topologies not reachable through tiny perturbations of the triangular patch. The best individual should be returned only after an exact distance check; if it has an upper-bound violation, radially contract all non-anchor points around the midpoint as a deterministic feasibility repair. This is a genuinely global alternative to the current local COBYLA basin search and is useful if the apparent reference configuration is not globally optimal.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Search for a higher-ratio contact topology and maximize the exact minimum squared distance while keeping the maximum distance at the anchored value one.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A raw 28-dimensional global search is expensive, so use workers=1 for determinism, a fixed seed, vectorized population evaluation, and a finite evaluation budget appropriate for the evaluator timeout. The penalty must dominate any apparent gain in minimum distance from a diameter violation. The anchor assumption is valid up to relabeling whenever an optimal configuration has a diameter pair, but the chosen bounding box must not accidentally exclude geometrically valid points.

tried_paradigms.idea: Freeze a high-precision contact-graph certificate as a static NumPy coordinate construction
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator has no requirement that optimization happen during evaluation: it imports the function and scores only the returned 16 by 2 array. The current program already spends runtime repeatedly solving a floating-point nonlinear program, then chooses whichever candidate has the best measured score; this introduces machine- and SciPy-version dependence and can lose score through final normalization. Use the current near-optimal output to identify its active contact graph offline, solve that fixed system to substantially higher precision outside the evaluated constructor, and store the resulting normalized coordinates as decimal float64 literals. The certificate should preserve every intended unit-diameter pair and give the shortest contacts a small positive clearance from accidental rounding changes. At runtime, the function should do only one numpy.asarray/numpy.array construction and return those immutable coordinates. This structural approach does not search for a new basin itself; its breakthrough value is that it converts any better solution found by a high-accuracy active-set solve into a deterministic, zero-optimization evaluator submission. It also permits systematic offline comparison of candidate contact graphs and choosing the one with the largest independently recomputed scipy.pdist ratio before freezing it. Because scoring is solely pairwise Euclidean distances, this static certificate is exactly equivalent to rerunning the optimizer but is far more numerically reproducible.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical robustness and retention of the best attainable squared ratio: eliminate COBYLA termination error, random-start dependence, post-normalization drift, and runtime failure risk while preserving a verified ratio above the benchmark.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not round coordinates aggressively: recompute all 120 float64 squared distances using the same SciPy/NumPy arithmetic expected by evaluation and retain at least 16 significant decimal digits. Ensure the stored set has exactly shape (16,2), dtype float64, no duplicated points, and no upper-distance violation caused by literal rounding. A static array only improves the score if the offline certificate is genuinely better than the current lattice-derived candidate; it is not a substitute for discovering that certificate.
